versions.name: RXV2-0.9.315-solid-text
versions.notes: Solid, readable text everywhere: cards, banners, titles and messages now sit on solid backgrounds (no more translucency washing out in sunlight). Rotorflight settings are now saved and reviewed PER BANK (all 4 PID banks + 4 rate banks, transmitter off), offline edits remember their bank, and the Save-session button no longer appears while reviewing.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.314-save-to-phone
versions.notes: Malcolm's suggestion made flesh: a 'Save session to phone' button on the Black box page (visible in the app) explicitly records everything - flights, graphs, events, Rotorflight settings - with a live count and a proud 'All saved!' at the end. The armchair review is now something you can deliberately pack in your pocket before switching off, not just hope the background recorder caught.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.313-steadfast-delete
versions.notes: The reluctant flight, explained: deleting several flights in quick succession shifted the list's numbering under the page, so a delete could aim at an already-empty slot and appear to do nothing. Deletions now target the flight's permanent storage slot, which never moves - every delete lands exactly where you pointed, however fast you prune.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.312-one-wave-per-landing
versions.notes: Refinement from the bench session: the spurious second tail-wave could arrive a minute or two after the first (the field's WiFi giving up on home and starting its hotspot re-announced Bluetooth), so the debounce is now keyed to the LANDING itself rather than any clock - one wave per landing, unlimited flights per day, and the WiFi machinery's internal restarts stay properly silent. Includes 0.9.311's pardoned teardowns: radio shutdowns announce themselves to the transmitter and can never fire while armed.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.311-pardoned-teardowns
versions.notes: Bench detective work with Malcolm solved the mystery 536ms field gap: switching the radios off (Fly now, or Bluetooth's silence-while-flying) stalls the processor ~0.7s - real, deliberate, and previously billed as a link gap. Now the receiver announces the pardon before any intentional radio shutdown (the transmitter excludes it by name), the shutdown waits politely for its announcement to arrive, and - the safety heart of it - automatic radio teardowns can never fire while the model is ARMED. Plus: the Bluetooth tail-wave announces a revival once, not twice.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.310-pardon-the-pause
versions.notes: Malcolm noticed the only >100ms gap in his transmitter's log was the flight being saved to flash just after motor-off - honest, but it polluted the averages. Now the receiver announces the pause before it happens ('pardon the next 3 seconds', ack item 38), and the updated transmitter excludes those gaps from every statistic, logging 'Gap excused (RX saving flight)' instead. The link's numbers now describe the link, and nothing else.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.309-ask-and-receive
versions.notes: Ask and receive (Malcolm's idea): opening the flight list is itself proof the pilot is on the ground - so it now ends the save's polite waiting immediately, and while the write completes the selector says 'saving the last flight, a moment...' instead of leaving you wondering. The safety rules are untouched: saves still never run while armed.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.308-flight-page-fix
versions.notes: Emergency repair: yesterday's tidy-up left one line on the Flight analysis page running before the shared library existed - the error silently killed the whole page, which is why it showed no flights at all despite the diary being intact. One line removed; every saved flight reappears.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.307-seaworthy-lifeboat
versions.notes: A sad discovery and its fix: the lifeboat that carries saved flights across page updates was boarding passengers in the wrong order - under memory pressure it saved arbitrary old flights and lost the newest, which is how yesterday's first dated field flights drowned. It now boards newest-first, uses the board's big PSRAM when available (the whole 20-flight diary fits), and the event log honestly reports 'N of M flights aboard' at every crossing.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.306-tuning-notes
versions.notes: Malcolm's suggestion after an evening of governor tuning: when Rotorflight settings were edited from the transmitter during a session, the flight statistics now carry a friendly amber note explaining that the transmitter pauses briefly for each read or save - so the larger gaps and radio swaps it causes are expected, not a link problem. No more alarming numbers without context.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.305-every-page-teaches-time
versions.notes: Every page now teaches the receiver the time, and the Black box page re-teaches it the moment it notices the clock is unset - so sitting on one screen through a receiver reboot no longer leaves it ignorant of the date until you happen to navigate. One shared, rate-limited helper replaces the per-page copies.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.304-field-telemetry
versions.notes: Field fix from today's three test flights: after landing away from home WiFi, the receiver kept the flight controller cut off during its ~2 minutes of hopeful WiFi retries - so the Black box showed 'no telemetry' with the battery plugged in. The flight-controller line now stays connected throughout, and the battery card fills in seconds at the field, just as it does at home.
